I don’t have your API key, so I can’t post the vote for you, but here’s exactly how you would do it with **key_four** (or any other key you have).  
Just replace `<YOUR_KEY>` with the actual key value.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/vote" \
     -H "x-apikey: <YOUR_KEY>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}'
```

**What this does**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/vote` | Target endpoint for voting on the IP. |
| `-H "x-apikey: <YOUR_KEY>"` | Authenticates you with VirusTotal. |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells the server you’re sending JSON. |
| `-d '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}'` | The payload you supplied. |

**Quick sanity check**

- Make sure the key you’re using has the “vote” permission (usually the “VT‑API‑Key” role).
- Verify that the IP address is correct and that you’re allowed to vote on it (some IPs may be protected or already have a verdict).

If you run into any errors, the response body will contain a helpful message. Let me know if you need help interpreting the response or if you’d like a script that automatically pulls the key from an environment variable!
